summary: Configured PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, node3 (standbys) on Ubuntu 16.04. Created a dedicated cluster CA on node1, issued server certs (CN=nodeX, SAN DNS/IP) for each node and one client cert (CN=replicator) for the replication role, deployed them to each node's data directory / postgres home. Enabled ssl=on with ssl_ca_file on all nodes, and restricted replication access in pg_hba.conf to `hostssl replication replicator <cluster-ip>/32 cert clientcert=1` — no other pg_hba rule matches replication connections, so plaintext or uncertified peers are rejected. Bootstrapped node2/node3 via pg_basebackup over TLS with sslmode=verify-full using the replicator client cert, configured recovery.conf with matching sslmode=verify-full/sslcert/sslkey/sslrootcert, and confirmed both standbys stream from node1 with pg_stat_ssl.ssl=t. Verified end-to-end data replication (INSERT on primary visible on both standbys) and proved cert-authority enforcement by attempting a connection with a self-signed (non-CA) cert bearing CN=replicator, which was rejected at the TLS handshake ('tlsv1 alert unknown ca'). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id/uptime and health baselines, restarted node2, node3, then node1 (primary last, preserving write availability as long as possible) one at a time via `systemctl reboot` with the acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled each node until reachable, confirmed each node's boot_id changed and uptime reset to 0, and verified PostgreSQL auto-restarted, replication state recovered (pg_is_in_recovery, pg_stat_replication streaming/async, ssl=t) and that a post-restart write on the primary replicated to both standbys.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 9.5 + contrib + openssl on node1, node2, node3
Set up cluster SSH (CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY) for inter-node scp
Created a cluster CA (ca.key/ca.crt) on node1
Issued server certs (CN=nodeX, SAN DNS/IP) for each node signed by the CA
Issued a client cert (CN=replicator) signed by the CA for replication auth
Distributed CA cert, per-node server certs, and replicator client cert to node2/node3 via scp
Installed certs into each node's PostgreSQL data directory with correct ownership/permissions

Configured postgresql.conf on all nodes: listen_addresses='*', ssl=on, ssl_cert_file/ssl_key_file/ssl_ca_file, wal_level=hot_standby, max_wal_senders=10, wal_keep_segments=64, hot_standby=on (fixed accidental hot_standby_feedback overwrite)
Configured pg_hba.conf on all nodes to accept replication connections only via hostssl ... cert clientcert=1 from the three cluster IPs
Created the replicator role with REPLICATION LOGIN on node1
Restarted node1 to apply config; fixed wal_level value from invalid 'replica' to valid 'hot_standby' for PG9.5
Wiped node2/node3 data directories and ran pg_basebackup from node1 over TLS (verify-full, client cert auth)
Restored server certs into node2/node3 data dirs post-basebackup and wrote recovery.conf with primary_conninfo using sslmode=verify-full and client cert paths
Started node2 and node3 as standbys and verified streaming replication state and pg_stat_ssl.ssl=t
Created repl_test table and inserted/verified data propagation to both standbys
Attempted replication connection with a self-signed non-CA client cert (CN=replicator) and confirmed TLS handshake rejection ('unknown ca')
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime and health baseline on all three nodes
Rebooted node2, node3, then node1 sequentially via systemctl reboot, confirming acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled each node until reachable and confirmed changed boot_id and uptime reset to 0 for each
Verified post-restart recovery: PostgreSQL online, correct pg_is_in_recovery state, replication streaming resumed over SSL, and new data (id=2) replicated to both standbys after primary restart

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured node1 (primary) -> node2, node3 (standbys)
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup succeeded over TLS for both standbys; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows node2/node3 streaming; pg_is_in_recovery=t on both standbys

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA created on node1 (ca.key/ca.crt), server certs issued per node, client cert for replicator issued; SHOW ssl = on; pg_stat_ssl confirms ssl=t for both replication connections

evidence.requirement: Only peers presenting a CA-issued certificate are accepted for replication
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts replication db to hostssl ... cert clientcert=1 only, no other matching rule; connection attempt with a self-signed non-CA cert (CN=replicator) was rejected with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca'
Row inserted on primary (node1) appeared on both node2 and node3 standbys
